summary: This is a test file that checks a RobotPet class using Python's built-in unittest framework. It creates a robot pet before each test and then verifies that its attributes are stored correctly and that show_talent() returns a string containing the pet's name.

lines.text: Brings in Python's standard testing framework, which supplies the test class and the assertion methods used below.
Pulls the class under test out of the pet_talents.py module; test files live separately from the code they exercise.
Inheriting from unittest.TestCase is what turns this class into a test suite: the framework finds it and runs every method whose name starts with test_.
setUp runs automatically before each individual test, so every test starts with a fresh object and cannot be affected by changes another test made.
Stores the freshly built pet on self so all the test methods can reach it.
Each test method takes self and gets its own run; the name should describe what is being checked.
assertEqual fails the test if the two values differ, confirming the constructor saved the name it was given.
A separate test for a separate behaviour, so a failure tells you exactly which expectation broke.
assertIn checks that the text appears somewhere inside the returned string, which is more flexible than demanding an exact sentence.
Verifies show_talent returns a string rather than printing and returning None, a common mistake in this kind of method.
Tests the class with a second, differently configured object to be sure the results really depend on the data passed in.
assertNotIn guards against the opposite error: a hard-coded name leaking into every pet's talent message.
This block only runs when the file is executed directly, so importing it elsewhere does not launch the tests.
Discovers every test method in the file, runs them, and prints a pass/fail summary.
